title: BPI Vgch 1 chinese cabbage: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: BPI Vgch 1 chinese cabbage: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: BPI Vgch 1 chinese cabbage is a chinese cabbage variety from BPI. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: BPI Vgch 1 is a registered chinese cabbage variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1983. BPI bred it. Its record notes 16.5 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about BPI Vgch 1 chinese cabbage
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 16.5 t/ha beats the average of its group, 12.68. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chinese cabbage fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant BPI Vgch 1 chinese cabbage

Pechay Baguio heads best in cool places. In the lowlands, pick a heat tolerant hybrid and plant in the cool months. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).
